newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures whipsaw late, end lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures whipsaw late, end lower.

text.p: U.S. debt futures absorbed a decent 30-year note auction near midday and set a new daily high, but quickly faltered there and ended lower.
September Treasury bonds rose to 115-6/32 just after results of the last of Treasury's $38.0 billion quarterly refunding, but soon fell to 115-1/32 and crumbled further.
Dealer sales amid thin pits and sell-stops exacerbated losses, taking September T-bonds to a more than two week low.
"The failure to maintain the uptick after the 30-year results was disappointing," said Don Pullen, bond trading floor manager with ED and F Man.
Treasury sold $10.0 billion in 30-year bonds at an average yield of 6.445 percent, with a bid-to-cover ratio of 2.66 and non-competitive bids at $332.6 million.

"I think the results of the 30-year was the best out of the three," said Rick Santelli, bond floor analyst for Rand Financial Services Inc. "The response to the auction was very good and we reached resistance at 115-5/32 to 6/32, but when the market started to give up a little bit of ground we saw a fairly decent offer from a dealer," he said.
ED and F Man's Pullen put support for Friday at 113-24/32.
Pullen said comments from Kansas City Federal Reserve President Thomas Hoenig may have added to the sell-off.
Hoenig said upside inflation risks exist in the U.S. economy given the low jobless rate. He also said central bankers still need to be cautious about inflation.
"So a combination of technical selling and bearish statements from Hoenig on inflation set the tone here for a weak close," Pullen said.
The market had held a persistent bid most of the day, even as the market priced a $3.0 billion Raytheon debt offering and awaited the bond auction.
A weaker-than-expected weekly jobless claims report had very minimal impact on the market early, further highlighting the early resilience in the market, traders said.
Claims rose to 300,000 in the week-ended August 2 from a revised 275,000 the prior week. Traders had expected a 307,000 reading.

At the close, September T-bonds were down 17/32 to 114-7/32, notes fell 7/32 to 109-18/32, munis fell 11/32 to 120-6/32, Eurodollars fell 0.015 to 94.070. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
